20. With regard to the legal issue, (a) as raised by the Bar it will be convenient and relevant to consider section 95 and 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 as amended up to date which runs as follows :- 

 21. It would not be unworthy to mention here that the legal history of legislation regarding the law of tenancy right and privilege the East Bengal Tenancy Act and the State acquisition and Tenancy Act were amended in the Indian Sub-continent, Erst-while Pakistan and thereafter in Bangladesh for the benefit of the tenants considering the social and economic conditions of the mass people. It is evident from the legal history that for the first time in the year 1929 Section 26G was introduced by amending Act IV of 1928, which came into force on 22-2-1929 the object of the legislature was to protect a raiyat, so that no raiyat can be ousted from possession of his land by a Mohajan wherein he is in possession for more then 15 years. Although in Section 58 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 defined "Mortgage", "mortgagee," "mortgage money" and "mortgage deed" but by amending Act VIII the Bengal Tenancy Act and in Act XXVIII of 1951 introduced a new section namely section 3(3) and 2 (6) respectively. The State Acquisition and Tenancy Act introduced definition of complete usufructuary mortgage", which says complete usufructuary mortgage means of transfer by a tenant of the right of possession in any land for the advanced or to be advanced by way of loan upon the condition that the loan with all interests thereon shall be deemed to be extinguished by the profits arising from the land during the period of Mortgage". Thereby all the raiyat were protected and relieved from all sorts of mortgages except the "complete usufructuary mortgage". Thereafter again sub-sections 4 and 5 in the Section 95 and thereafter 95A were added in the State Acquisition & Tenancy Act,1950 by President's Order No. 88 of 1972, from which it is crystal clear that in the eye of law, no conditional mortgage is valid and any sale with condition of reconvey is a "complete usufructuary mortgage."
